chunks.text: Today we will talk about Niger.
Niger is a large, dry, and friendly country in West Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Niger?
Niger is in West Africa.
It is next to Nigeria, Chad, Algeria, Libya, Burkina Faso, Mali, and Benin.
It is a landlocked country, which means it has no sea.
Much of Niger is part of the Sahara Desert.
What is the capital city of Niger?
The capital city is Niamie.
Niamie is by the Niger River.
It has markets, schools, offices, and mosques.
It is the largest city in the country.
Other towns include Agades, an old desert city.
Maradi, a farming and trade center.
Zender and Tahua.
How many people live in Niger?
About 25 million people live in Niger.
Many people live in villages and rural areas.
Niger has a young population.
Most people are under 20 years old.
What language do people speak in Niger?
The official language is French.
But many people speak local African languages such as Hazarma Tamashak, Tuareg language.
Fulfulda.
People often speak two or three languages.
What is the weather like in Niger?
Niger is one of the hottest countries in the world.
It has a hot dry season from February to May.
A short rainy season from June to September.
A cooler dry season from October to January.
Rain is rare, especially in the north.
What does Niger look like?
Niger has desert land with sand and rocks.
The Niger River in the southwest, mountains in the north like the air mountains, savannas and dry grasslands in the south.
It is a land of sun, wind and wide open space.
What animals live in Niger?
In Niger you can find camels, goats and donkeys, lizards, snakes and scorpions, birds like eagles and guinea fowl.
In some parks, antelopes, giraffes and elephants, Niger is home to the last wild giraffes in West Africa.
What do people eat in Niger?
Nigerian food is simple, local and made for hot weather.
People eat millet and sorghum, grains used for porridge, rice and maize, beans, leafy greens and onions, meat like goat, beef and chicken.
Popular dishes, tuwo, millet porridge served with sauce, Jalaf rice, rice with tomato and spices, fried dough balls, grilled meat with chili.
People often eat with their hands sitting together on mats.
What do people drink in Niger?
People drink water.
In Niger, tea, green tea with sugar is very popular.
Milk, especially from goats or cows, juice from hibiscus, baobab or ginger.
In villages, people sit and share three rounds of tea with friends.
What is life like in Niger?
Life in Niger is often rural, traditional and community based.
People enjoy farming and herding animals, helping family and visiting neighbors, going to the mosque, dancing, music and storytelling.
Resting in the shade during the hot day, many people wear light flowing clothes to stay cool.
What are some holidays and traditions in Niger?

Independence Day, August 3rd, Eid al -Fitr at the end of Ramadan, Eid al -Adha, the Festival of Sacrifice, traditional weddings and naming ceremonies, music festivals in the desert, especially among the Tuareg people.
Festivals include camel races, drums and colorful clothing.
Some fun facts about Niger.
Niger is named after the Niger River.
The Tuareg people are known as blue men of the desert.
The Sahara covers over 80 % of the country.
Niger has uranium mines important for its economy.
The national flag is orange, white and green with an orange circle.
Now you know many things about Niger.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the desert, traditions and daily life.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Amili.
